sources.title: Chief ministers: birth date, Lahore origin and provincial terms
sources.findings: Punjab official list gives birth 23 September 1951 and Lahore as place of origin, plus chief-minister periods 20 February 1997–12 October 1999, 8 June 2008–27 March 2013 and 7 June 2013–7 June 2018. It omits the 2009 interruption. Provincial assembly decisions separately cite 6 June 2013 assumption, a one-day discrepancy: profile uses 2013 year precision rather than choosing an unsupported exact date. Third-term endpoint is also kept at year precision.

sources.title: Prime minister profile: education, earlier offices and oath on 4 March 2024
sources.findings: Toronto consulate heading confirms oath on 4 March 2024 and prior premiership April 2022–August 2023. Read Government College Lahore graduation, 1985 chamber presidency, provincial assembly 1988, National Assembly 1990, provincial opposition 1993 and chief-minister history. No subject, degree level or graduation year given. Older body says opposition leader and party president from 2018 to April 2022: not evidence of current party presidency or opposition role. Nawaz is his brother, a different premier. Promotional adjectives are omitted.

sources.title: Orders and proceedings, 11 April 2022: election of prime minister
sources.findings: Original National Assembly proceedings of 11 April 2022 record election with 174 votes, announced at 5:02 pm. Qureshi had announced withdrawal; zero votes recorded for him are not interpreted as a universal vote against his party. Document confirms parliamentary election, not a separate oath ceremony. First-term end is only August 2023 from consulate; no invented exact end date.

sources.title: Orders and proceedings, 3 March 2024: 201 and 92 votes
sources.findings: Original National Assembly proceedings of 3 March 2024 record 201 for Sharif and 92 for Omer Ayub, with declaration at 1:43 pm. Parliamentary voting, election declaration and next-day oath are distinct. Avoids inconsistent ordinal prime-minister numbering and does not represent these as nationwide popular votes.

sources.title: 12 July 2023: nine-month US$3 billion Stand-By Arrangement
sources.findings: Read IMF 12 July 2023 Board announcement: nine-month SBA of SDR2.250 billion, approximately US$3 billion; SDR894 million/about US$1.2 billion immediately available, remainder phased subject to two quarterly reviews. Approval is not full payment, a grant or personal wealth. Distinct from 2024 EFF.

sources.title: 25 September 2024 Board approval of 37-month Extended Fund Facility
sources.findings: Read IMF release dated 27 September 2024 covering Board action on 25 September: 37-month EFF of SDR5.320 billion/about US$7 billion; SDR760 million/about US$1 billion immediately available. Fiscal, energy and governance reforms, social protection and continuing vulnerabilities are noted; no assertion that all funds arrived immediately, debt problems ended or forecasts became actual 2026 results.

sources.title: 2024 prime-minister election, coalition and disputed general-election context
sources.findings: Read AP 2024 election report for coalition context, first premiership after Imran Khan government fell, and PTI allegations about the preceding general election alongside election-authority denial. Allegations are not adopted as proven fraud or a judicial verdict. The official parliamentary tally is independently confirmed by primary proceedings.

sources.publisher: Presidency of Türkiye, Directorate of Communications
sources.title: Erdoğan–Sharif meeting in Antalya, 12 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Turkish presidency communications account dated 12 November 2026: actual Erdoğan–Sharif meeting in Antalya during COP31. This is a completed encounter, not merely a travel itinerary. No unverified wider diplomatic or peace-settlement claims imported.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Pakistan
sources.title: 13 November 2026 report on previous day’s meeting with Erdoğan
sources.findings: Read Pakistan MOIB report published 13 November 2026 describing previous Thursday’s meeting, 12 November, and trade, investment, defence, energy and connectivity discussion. Reproduces prime-minister-office information; it is Pakistan’s official account rather than an independent press eyewitness. Combined with Turkish record for reciprocal confirmation. Intentions and planned cooperation are not completed projects.

sources.title: Punjab Assembly Decisions 2000–2014: chief-minister offices and 2009 Governor’s Rule
sources.findings: Read selected chief-minister notes in Punjab Assembly Decisions 2000–2014, printed pp. xxviii–xxix, with government notification references: 8 June 2008 assumption; Governor’s Rule introduced 25 February 2009 caused ministers to cease office, revoked 30 March. Revocation is not automatically the exact personal reinstatement date. Document gives 6 June 2013 for renewed office versus 7 June on modern CM list; profile retains year precision. Full 2015 compilation not exhaustively reviewed.
